newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh seeks to bring back share investors.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh seeks to bring back share investors.

text.p: Bangladesh's main Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) is expected to resume trading on Tuesday after the government and business leaders agreed on providing necessary incentives to hundreds of striking investors.

Market sources said on Monday that the Federation of Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Dhaka Stock Exchange and Chittagong Stock Exchange suggested a package of incentives to restore investor confidence.

These include resumption of credit to investors by state-owned Investment Corporation of Bangladesh and formation of committees to oversee share price movement and ensure transparency in transactions.
"The government has accepted all the proposals and these will be implemented on an emergency basis," Shah Abdul Hannan, a finance ministry secretary, said.
"The central bank will ensure adequate financing to reactivate the market," Hannan told reporters after a meeting with the business leaders.
Trading on the DSE has been suspended since Sunday as hundreds of small investors in the kerb market staged demonstration outside the DSE building preventing stock brokers from entering the floor.
The DSE all share price index closed 48.8 points or 1.83 percent down at 2,618.3 on Saturday. Friday is the weekend in Moslem Bangladesh.
